planting.note: Propagate 'Monkey Wings' exclusively by division in spring, since seedlings often revert to the straight species' smooth-edged leaflets; plant divisions immediately into consistently moist, humus-rich, neutral woodland soil in partial to full shade.

directions: Propagate 'Monkey Wings' exclusively by division in spring, since seedlings often revert to the straight species' smooth-edged leaflets; plant divisions immediately into consistently moist, humus-rich, neutral woodland soil in partial to full shade. This distinctive selection of the native twinleaf was discovered and named for its gently lobed, wing-like leaflet margins, a departure from the smooth-edged foliage typical of the species, and was first propagated and introduced by Quackin' Grass Nursery in Connecticut. Solitary white, eight-petaled flowers open on leafless stalks in early spring before the paired leaflets fully expand, and the foliage matures over the following weeks from about 8 inches tall at bloom time to as much as 18 inches once the seed capsules ripen. Site it alongside other spring ephemerals in a shaded woodland border where the soil stays reliably moist and richly organic, and avoid disturbing established clumps once they take hold.

planting.note: Plant divisions in early spring into moist, humus-rich, neutral to slightly alkaline woodland soil in partial to full shade, giving this rare white-flowered selection the same cool, undisturbed conditions favored by the lavender-flowered species.

directions: Plant divisions in early spring into moist, humus-rich, neutral to slightly alkaline woodland soil in partial to full shade, giving this rare white-flowered selection the same cool, undisturbed conditions favored by the lavender-flowered species. 'Alba' is a scarce sport of Asian twinleaf bearing pure white, cup-shaped flowers instead of the typical lavender-blue, opening from April into May above kidney-shaped leaves that emerge flushed reddish-orange before maturing to blue-green. Like the species it is slow to establish and best left undisturbed once settled, gradually forming a long-lived clump over many years. Pair it with hellebores, trilliums, and other choice woodland companions in a shaded collector's bed with consistent moisture.

planting.note: Plant divisions in fall or very early spring into deep, moist, humus-rich, acidic soil in partial shade, choosing the coolest and most sheltered site available since this white-flowered form is, if anything, more demanding than the species.

directions: Plant divisions in fall or very early spring into deep, moist, humus-rich, acidic soil in partial shade, choosing the coolest and most sheltered site available since this white-flowered form is, if anything, more demanding than the species. 'Alba' produces the same deeply divided, anemone-like foliage as the species but sends up nodding, pure white cup-shaped flowers in mid to late summer instead of the typical lilac-mauve, an especially rare sport among specialty woodland growers. Because seedlings can revert toward the species' normal coloring, propagate only by careful division of an established clump to keep the white form true. Give it a permanently moist, richly organic pocket alongside hostas, ferns, and other choice shade perennials, and avoid disturbing the roots once the clump is settled.

planting.note: Plant divisions in fall or very early spring into deep, moist, humus-rich, acidic soil in full shade, siting this selection in the coolest, most sheltered pocket of the woodland garden available.

directions: Plant divisions in fall or very early spring into deep, moist, humus-rich, acidic soil in full shade, siting this selection in the coolest, most sheltered pocket of the woodland garden available. 'Double Flower' bears extra petal-like segments on its nodding, waxy blossoms, giving each flower a fuller, more complex form than the single lilac-mauve cups of the species, with blooms carrying a light blue-pink tinge over white in mid to late summer. As with other named Anemonopsis selections, propagate by division rather than seed to preserve the doubled flower structure, since seed-grown offspring typically revert to the plain single-flowered species. Provide constant moisture, a deep humus-rich mulch, and protection from root disturbance, since established clumps resent being divided except for deliberate propagation.
